pitch: The automation layer that connects your products: pick an event, add conditions, choose the action, and let the platform do the follow-up, with a record of every run and an AI assistant that answers from your own data.
overview:
Business Automation is how the products work together instead of side by side. A Super Admin builds rules in the Workspace: choose an event from the products your company uses, narrow it with conditions, and decide what happens next. Actions can send an email, notify a person or everyone with a role, or call a signed webhook so your own systems can react.

Start from a ready-made template or build from scratch, send a test with sample values before turning a rule on, and open the run history to see what fired and what each action did. Around the rules sit the pieces that make a connected company work: one sign-in and role model across every product, search across your records, a notifications bell, an activity trail, CSV import, and an assistant that answers questions from your own data.

A company starts by registering itself, goes through the Workspace set-up, and then manages its plan, trial and billing itself. Each company's data and automations are kept separate from every other company's.
outcome: Hand-offs happen without anyone having to remember them, and the company can see what ran, when and with what result.

faq.q: Is there an approval workflow?
faq.a: SOPs move from draft to published to active without a separate approval step. Authors and managers publish directly, within their permissions.

faq.q: Can sensitive SOPs be restricted?
